parts.modelAnswer: American silver drove prices up in Spain and across Europe. More silver money chased the same goods, so prices rose.
parts.prompt: Identify one effect of American silver on Spain's economy.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for identifying one accurate effect on Spain's economy, such as rising prices, higher taxes, or growing debt.
scoring.notEarned: Naming silver mining without stating an effect on Spain's economy does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The crown spent the silver on armies, wars, and interest payments rather than investing it in farms or workshops. A tiny landowning class saw no reason to modernize, so the wealth passed through Spain instead of building its economy.
parts.prompt: Explain why the silver did not make Spain richer.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate reason the silver did not enrich Spain, such as spending on war, debt, inflation, or the landowning class's lack of investment.
scoring.notEarned: Restating that Spain stayed poor, without explaining why, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Silver set off a long wave of inflation across Western Europe, raising prices everywhere the money circulated. It also funded an arms race, as Spain's large army forced its rivals to multiply their own forces.
parts.prompt: Explain one effect of American silver on Europe beyond Spain.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate effect beyond Spain, such as inflation across Europe or the arms race among rival powers.
scoring.notEarned: Naming an effect inside Spain only does not earn the point.

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 3, The Economic Impact of Conquest. Distinct angle from MCQ set silver-paradox.
stimulus.text: American silver flowed into Spain through the 1500s, yet the crown grew poorer rather than richer. Taxes rose more than fivefold to pay for armies and wars, and the crown borrowed heavily from European bankers. At the same time, prices rose across Europe as the supply of silver money grew. The silver arrived in Seville and left again, spent on soldiers, ships, and interest.
